title: Rio Grande Onion (Rio Grande F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Rio Grande onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Rio Grande onion is an F1 hybrid onion variety, also sold or known as Rio Grande F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: Onion plants in beds separated by grassy paths on a Philippine farm, the kind of farm where Rio Grande onion is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Rio Grande F1, this is the same onion. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [onion variety finder](/crop-varieties/onion), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for onion and garlic](/land-preparation/onion-garlic-land-preparation).
Key facts about Rio Grande onion

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources
rows: Days to harvest, per the seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: harvest 80 to 85 days after transplanting. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit onion fields most often: [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [onion armyworm](/pests/onion-armyworm), [purple blotch of onion](/diseases/purple-blotch), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** Harvest 80 to 85 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Bulb: firm, even, bright yellow bulbs of 130 to 150 g.
Rated intermediate against leaf miner, twisting, damping off, purple blotch and bulb rot.

blocks.text: These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual onion on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Rio Grande onion

Red onion stores longer, while yellow onion yields more. Pick a variety that bulbs in the short days of the Philippine dry season, and plant it after the rains so the bulbs dry well. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Rio Grande F1 the same as Rio Grande?
items.a: Yes. Rio Grande F1 is another name for Rio Grande. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Rio Grande?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
